name: 甘味カフェ 茶ゆ (Kanmi Cafe Chayu)

claims.text: Signature sweets are served in wheat-based monaka wafers and dorayaki; no gluten-free handling or allergen control is documented for the shared sweets kitchen.

The shop centers on dairy gelato made with Noto/Ishikawa milk; sorbets and gelato are likely scooped and prepared with shared equipment, so dairy cross-contact for plant-based diners is not addressed.
Fruit sorbets such as Noto Yanagida blueberry and seasonal Kanazawa watermelon are listed as plant-based flavors, giving non-dairy diners at least some options.

name: 甘味処 金花糖 (Kanmidokoro Kinkato)

claims.text: Signature anmitsu dishes are typically served with the shop's homemade dairy ice cream, so plant-based diners should ask for it to be omitted.
Core components are made in-house (anko from Tamba Dainagon beans, shiratama, kanten, ice cream), so ingredients are simple and known to the makers.

name: 川端鮮魚店 片町店 (Kawabata Sengyoten Katamachi-ten)

claims.text: Sashimi and grilled seafood are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free tamari is documented.
Menu is centered on fish and shellfish with fish-based dashi; no vegan-safe preparations are documented.
As a Kaga-cuisine kaiseki ryotei, menus rely on dashi and soy-based seasonings; no allergen or gluten information is published, so wheat-containing soy sauce should be assumed present.
Courses are built around sashimi, grilled fish and simmered seafood alongside dashi, so animal ingredients and cross-contact are pervasive on the standard menus.
Meals are served in private rooms by reservation, so dietary requests can in principle be discussed directly with the kitchen when booking ahead.

name: 季節おでん じゅん (Kisetsu Oden Jun)

claims.text: The shared oden pot simmers wheat-containing items (kuruma-fu wheat gluten, house-made fishcakes) in the same soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, so all items share gluten-laden liquid — there is no way to avoid cross-contamination for a single broth pot.
The dashi is finished with Kanazawa's Ohno soy sauce (大野醤油), a standard wheat-fermented Japanese soy sauce, used throughout the broth.
The base broth is a bonito (katsuobushi) and kombu dashi, so even vegetable items are simmered in fish-derived stock.

name: 季節料理・おでん 黒百合 (Kisetsu Ryori Oden Kuroyuri)

claims.text: Oden is simmered communally in a shared dashi pot that includes wheat-based items such as fried gluten/fu cakes, so all oden shares broth with gluten-containing ingredients.
The oden broth and seasonings are soy-sauce based; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
The base broth is a fish/bonito dashi and the menu is seafood-centric, so vegetable items are cooked in animal-derived stock.

name: キッチンユキ 武蔵店 (Kitchen Yuki Musashi-ten)

claims.text: Japanese curry roux is thickened with wheat flour and the signature cutlets are coated in wheat breadcrumbs and deep-fried, so the core menu is inherently wheat-based.
The curry sauce and menu are meat-based (pork and chicken cutlets, hayashi rice), with no documented vegetarian or vegan preparation.

name: 小料理とおでん 燗九郎 (Koryori to Oden Kankuro)

claims.text: Oden and small-plate izakaya cooking in Japan standardly uses wheat-containing soy sauce and dashi; no gluten-free preparation is documented for this kitchen.

Broths are animal-based (duck-bone stock; bonito and dried-fish/shiitake dashi) and signature items center on fish, scallop, egg and meat, so vegan dishes and avoidance of animal cross-contact are not provided.
